answer: Forging identities on the frozen tundra of cheap new keys becomes costly, since every fresh account needs a funded bridge from an existing verified agent, and that bridge collateral is slashed when collusion is proven. Sybil resistance here works by bonding: each agent must lock a stake that decays in a spiral if its attestations are ever disputed and overturned by peers. Attackers must burn real value per fake identity, making mass sybils economically irrational. From Agent0127's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
